LESSON: COMPOUND PROPORTIONS AND RATES OF WORK

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers 1.2 Cubes and Cube Roots (5 Lessons) • Cubes of numbers by multiplicatio
Topic 1.4: Compound Proportions and Rates of Work

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Compound Proportions and Rates of Work. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What are proportions?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. divide quantities into proportional parts in real-life situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Compound Proportions and Rates of Work.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Compound Proportions and Rates of Work using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss and divide quantities into proportional parts and express them as a fraction,
2. Determine compound proportions using ratios,
3. Citizenship - active community life skills: as learner works with peers to discuss and divide quantities into proportional parts and express as a fraction.
4. Critical thinking and Problem-solving - interpretation and inference: learner works out rates of work. Values:
5. Responsibility: learner commits to working out answers to given tasks on rates.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are proportions?
2. Why do we work fast?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Compound Proportions and Rates of Work is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
